requirement: Represent a half-open stepped range of dates that can be iterated repeatedly, reports its length rounded up, and answers membership arithmetically, rejecting non-positive steps and a stop before start.
skeleton: DateRange class validating in __init__, a generator __iter__ over a local cursor, a ceiling-division __len__, and an arithmetic __contains__ that excludes non-dates and datetimes.
caption: A re-iterable container of dates built with the standard-library datetime module and collections.abc Iterator, as opposed to a one-shot iterator. DateRange(start, stop, step_days=1) raises ValueError saying step_days must be at least 1, and ValueError saying stop must not be before start; equal start and stop give an empty range. It keeps start, stop and step_days unchanged for its whole life. __iter__ is a generator that copies start into a local cursor and yields dates while the cursor is strictly before stop, advancing by a timedelta of step_days days, so every call to iter produces a fresh independent iterator and nested loops over the same range work. __len__ returns the day span divided by step_days rounded up, so a partial final step still counts and len agrees with iteration. __contains__ returns False for anything that is not a date and for datetime instances, which subclass date, and otherwise checks that the day offset from start is at least zero, below the span and a multiple of step_days, without iterating. The fixture asserts that January 1 to 8 every 3 days yields the 1st, 4th and 7th while ending on the 7th excludes it, that the same range can be listed twice and nested, that lengths are 3, 2 and 0 and match iteration for a February range, that membership is true only for the 4th among several dates, a datetime and a string, and that both invalid ranges raise ValueError.

plan.intent: Loop over calendar dates more than once
constraints: Invalid steps and a stop before start raise ValueError
Iteration excludes stop and can be repeated or nested
Length counts a partial final step
Membership honours the step and rejects datetimes and non-dates
The range never mutates its own bounds

rationale.teaches: Making a class iterable with a generator __iter__ over local state, plus __len__ and __contains__ computed arithmetically.
rationale.why: Advancing state stored on the object turns a container into a one-shot iterator that is silently empty the second time, and off-by-one bounds only show at the edges.

ops.docstring: A half-open range of dates that can be iterated any number of times.

ops.stmt: from datetime import date, datetime, timedelta

candidates.why_wrong: Advancing self.start consumes the range, so a second iteration yields nothing.
The loop includes stop, so a range ending exactly on a step yields one date too many.
Floor division drops the partial final step, so len disagrees with iteration.
Membership ignores the step, so dates between steps are reported as contained.
A step of zero is accepted, which would make iteration loop forever.
